protocol.title: UAV Computer Vision for Precision Agriculture: Deep Learning Segmentation & Edge Inference Benchmark Review

research_questions.text: What is the comparative segmentation performance (mIoU, F1-score) of CNNs, Transformers, and Hybrid architectures on agricultural UAV crop-weed imagery, specifically in paired intra-study benchmarks?

How do edge hardware constraints (thermal design power, compute capacity in TOPS) and execution configurations (quantization precision, input resolution) impact real-time inference throughput (FPS, latency) for UAV segmentation models?

inclusion.criterion: Focuses on deep learning architectures (CNN, Transformer, or Hybrid) applied to UAV aerial imagery for agricultural crop/weed pixel-level segmentation.
Reports quantitative pixel-wise segmentation accuracy metrics (e.g., mIoU, class IoU, Dice/F1-score) on agricultural benchmark or custom UAV datasets.
Reports on-device empirical hardware execution metrics (e.g., FPS, latency in ms, power in Watts, memory footprint) on physical edge platforms or embedded accelerators.

exclusion.criterion: Non-UAV imaging modalities (satellite-only, ground-vehicle/tractor-only, or laboratory bench-top setups without aerial flight context).
Bounding-box object detection or whole-image classification without pixel-level semantic or instance segmentation masks.
Agricultural domains outside crop and weed management (e.g., orchard fruit counting, forestry canopy height, livestock tracking, soil moisture estimation).
Exclusively non-deep learning methods (e.g., classical vegetation indices like ExG/NDVI with Otsu thresholding or shallow SVM without learned features).
Secondary literature without primary empirical benchmarks (surveys, systematic reviews, viewpoint letters, or tutorials).
Non-English text or records lacking retrievable quantitative results.

papers.title: Edge AI Method of Weed Detection and Removal in Paddy Field
papers.abstract: Increasing need for sustainable agriculture yield, maintenance and food security requires innovative methods in weed management, particularly in labor-intensive paddy crops. This paper presents a novel and optimal framework for real-time detection and removal of weeds in paddy fields using Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) technologies. Conventional methods, mostly rely on manual labor to detect and remove the weeds. The proposed system integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) installed on edge devices to empower immediate decision-making in the arena. To distinguish between rice plants and common aggressive weeds such as barnyard grass and jungle rice the model is trained, even under challenging situations like similar morphology or even under variable climatic factors. Real-time processing is accomplished with lightweight AI models enhanced for edge positioning on devices like NVIDIA Jetson Nano, drones, robots and Raspberry Pi with AI accelerators. Field examinations prove that a significant reduction in herbicide use, improved detection accuracy (up to 92%), and greater operational efficiency when compared to traditional methods. The proposed study authorizes that Edge AI offers an environmentally friendly, scalable and economically feasible solution which yields more crops for precision agriculture in rice farming.
papers.venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)

papers.title: Effect of multi-level and multi-scale spectral data source on vineyard state assessment via spectral vegetation indices
papers.abstract: Currently, the main goal of agriculture is to promote the resilience of agricultural systems in a sustainable way through the improvement of use efficiency of farm resources, increasing crop yield and quality, under climate change conditions. Climate change is one of the major challenges for high incomes crops, as the vineyards for high-quality wines, since it is expected to drastically modify plant growth, with possible negative effects especially in arid and semi-arid regions of Europe. In this context, the reduction of negative environmental impacts of intensive agriculture (e.g. soil degradation), can be realized by means of high spatial and temporal resolution of field crop monitoring, aiming to manage the local spatial variability.The monitoring of spatial behaviour of plants during the growing season represents an opportunity to improve the plant management, the farmer incomes and to preserve the environmental health, but it represents an additional cost for the farmer.The UAS-based imagery might provide detailed and accurate information across visible and near infrared spectral regions to support monitoring (crucial for precision agriculture) with limitation in bands and then on spectral vegetation indices (Vis) provided. VIs are a well-known and widely used method for crop state estimation. The ability to monitor crop state by such indices is an important tool for agricultural management. While differences in imagery and point-based spectroscopy are obvious, their impact on crop state estimation by VIs is not well-studied. The aim of this study was to assess the performance level of the selected VIs calculated from reconstructed high-resolution satellite (Sentinel-2A) multispectral imagery (13 bands across 400-2500nm with spatial resolution of The test site is a portion of vineyard placed in southern Italy cultivated on Greco cultivar, in which the soil-plant and atmosphere system has been monitored during the 2020 vintage also through ecophysiological analyses. The data analysis will follow the methodology presented in a recently published paper (Polinova et al., 2018).The study will connect the method and scale of spectral data collection with in vivo plant monitoring and prove that it has a significant impact on the vegetation state estimation results. It should be noted that each spectral data source has its advantages and drawbacks. The plant parameter of interest should determine not only the VIs type suitable for analysis but also the method of data collection.The contribution has been realized within the CNR BIO-ECO project.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Weed Detection and Segmentation in Agricultural Crops Using Images Captured by an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has changed how processes are developed, and decisions are made in the agricultural area replacing manual and repetitive processes with automated and more efficient ones. This study presents the application of deep learning techniques to detect and segment weeds in agricultural crops by applying models with different architectures in the analysis of images captured by an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). This study contributes to the computer vision field by comparing the performance of the You Only Look Once (YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s, YOLOv8m, and YOLOv8l), Mask R-CNN (with framework Detectron2), and U-Net models, making public the dataset with aerial images of soybeans and beans. The models were trained using a dataset consisting of 3021 images, randomly divided into test, validation, and training sets, which were annotated, resized, and increased using the Roboflow application interface. Evaluation metrics were used, which included training efficiency (mAP50 and mAP50-90), precision, accuracy, and recall in the model’s evaluation and comparison. The YOLOv8s variant achieved higher performance with an mAP50 of 97%, precision of 99.7%, and recall of 99% when compared to the other models. The data from this manuscript show that deep learning models can generate efficient results for automatic weed detection when trained with a well-labeled and large set. Furthermore, this study demonstrated the great potential of using advanced object segmentation algorithms in detecting weeds in soybean and bean crops.
papers.venue: Remote Sensing

papers.title: Advancing Smart Farming with UAV-Based Deep Learning for Proactive Wheat Disease Management
papers.abstract: Wheat diseases are a huge risk to the food security of the world and can result in extreme yield loss in case they are not diagnosed and treated at an early stage. Previously, disease identification required manual scanning, which is labor intensive, time-consuming, and inaccurate. The project shows a real-time, scalable, and automated wheat disease detection system with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), multispectral sensing, and deep learning. The system described above is unlike the conventional ground-based methods, the model uses aerial imagery collected using UAVs in conjunction with deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), specifically fine-tuned VGG19, to enhance scalability and accuracy. Grad-CAM visualization is also integrated to make predictions from models interpretable by farmers. In addition, the system incorporates real-time processing as well as IoT for automated early disease intervention alerting. The combination of large-scale monitoring, high-accuracy disease detection, and farmer-friendly deployment, this project fills important gaps in existing research with a pioneering, field-application solution for precision agriculture. Experimental results show high detection accuracy, proving its robustness under varying environmental conditions. This technology allows farmers to obtain real-time information, enabling timely disease management and sustainable wheat production.
papers.venue: 2025 Fourth International Conference on Smart Technologies, Communication and Robotics (STCR)

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Hybrid System for Autonomous Pest Detection and Control in Sustainable Agriculture Using IoT and Drone Networks
papers.abstract: In this work, a hybrid system based on reinforcement learning is presented for autonomous pest identification and management in sustainable agriculture through the use of drone networks and the Internet of Things. To increase the effectiveness of pest control, the suggested approach combines machine learning methods with aerial surveillance and real-time environmental monitoring. Drones take high-resolution pictures to identify pests, while IoT sensors continually gather field data like temperature, humidity, and crop conditions. By optimizing decision-making for targeted pesticide application, a reinforcement learning algorithm minimizes resource waste and its negative effects on the environment. The model is compared to conventional methods such as CNN-based models, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Logistic Regression. With an accuracy of 96.8% and an AUC of 98.0%, experimental data show that the suggested hybrid model performs better. By providing intelligent, automated, and scalable pest management solutions for modern farming systems, this method improves precision agriculture methods.
papers.venue: International Conference on Circuit, Power and Computing Technologies

papers.title: High‐Performance Deep Learning for Instant Pest and Disease Detection in Precision Agriculture
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Global farm productivity is constantly under attack from pests and diseases, resulting in massive crop loss and food insecurity. Manual scouting, expert estimation, and laboratory‐based microscopy are time‐consuming, prone to human error, and labor‐intensive. Although traditional machine learning classifiers such as SVM, Random Forest, and Decision Trees provide better accuracy, they are not field deployable. This article presents a high‐performance deep learning fusion model using MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 for real‐time detection of pests and diseases in precision farming. The model, trained on the CCMT dataset (24,881 original and 102,976 augmented images in 22 classes of cashew, cassava, maize, and tomato crops), attained a global accuracy of 89.5%, precision and recall of 95.68%, F1‐score of 95.67%, and ROC‐AUC of 0.95. For supporting deployment in edge environments, methods such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation were employed to decrease inference time to below 10 ms per image. The suggested model is superior to baseline CNN models, including ResNet‐50 (81.25%), VGG‐16 (83.10%), and other edge lightweight models (83.00%). The optimized model is run on low‐power devices such as smartphones, Raspberry Pi, and farm drones without the need for cloud computing, allowing real‐time detection in far‐off fields. Field trials using drones validated rapid image capture and inference performance. This study delivers a scalable, cost‐effective, and accurate early pest and disease detection framework for sustainable agriculture and supporting food security at the global level. The model has been successfully implemented with TensorFlow Lite within Android applications and Raspberry Pi systems.
papers.venue: Food Science & Nutrition

papers.title: Deep Transformer-Based Visual Framework for Early Detection of Plant Leaf Pathologies
papers.abstract: Accurate and quick detection of plant leaf diseases is essential for precision agriculture to intervene promptly and boost crop yields. A new deep learning model called ResVNet has been introduced in this study. It combines the powerful local feature detection of ResNet152 with the global attention capabilities of Vision Transformer (ViT) and utilises Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to accelerate fine-tuning. The PlantVillage dataset, which contains both healthy and diseased tomato samples, was used to train and test ResVNet. Experimental evaluation on the PlantVillage tomato dataset using stratified 5-fold cross-validation demonstrates that the proposed ResVNet model achieves a mean classification accuracy of 97.45%, along with superior macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1 scores compared to existing deep learning architectures. The results of the confusion matrix and the ROC analysis validate its discriminatory power. The results highlight the potential of architectures strengthened with transformers in agricultural diagnostics. For real-time disease detection in the field, ResVNet is perfect for edge device deployment on drones and smartphones thanks to its high accuracy and adaptability. The application of Explainable AI (XAI) technologies for interpretability, integration with the Internet of Things (IoT), and multi-crop classification will all be explored in future studies. We will also look into model compression approaches so we can deploy efficiently in low-resource settings without sacrificing performance.
papers.venue: Tarım Bilimleri Dergisi

papers.title: Deep Learning Based Precision Agriculture System for Automated Crop Disease Detection and Classification Using Drone Imagery
papers.abstract: The rise in agricultural sector requires novel approaches to overcome the challenges of crop disease detection which has a great impact on the productivity and sustainability. In this study, the researcher hypothesizes a Deep Learning-Based Precision Agriculture System, which will combine drone image with sophisticated Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to identify and classify crop diseases automatically. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) were used to take high-resolution aerial images with an RGB and multispectral camera. Several deep learning models (AlexNet, VGG16, ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0) were preprocessed and augmented and trained and tested. EfficientNetB0 was the most accurate with 97.5, surpassing the classical machine learning algorithms (SVM and Random Forest). Real-time accuracy was seen in the field deployment of 95.8, inference time of 0.45 seconds per image and a 28 percent decrease in the use of pesticides. The suggested system will allow identifying diseases at an initial stage, reducing human intervention, and facilitate a data-driven decision-making in farming. The combination of deep learning with UAV technology can provide scalability, cost, and sustainability of smart farming. This paper concludes that the system has the potential of greatly enhancing the efficiency of crop management and it becomes the foundation of further studies on the integration of IoT and predictive analytics to carry out large scale agriculture monitoring.
papers.venue: 2025 4th International Conference on Applied Artificial Intelligence and Computing (ICAAIC)

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Deep Learning and Sensor-based Approaches for Efficient Mango Disease Detection
papers.abstract: Mango is an important fruit crop that grown all over the world, but its production is severely challenged by for leaf and fruit diseases such as anthracnose, powdery mildew, bacterial canker, and stem rot. This review summarises the findings of 20 peer-reviewed research papers, systematically reviewed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and MetaAnalyses (PRISMA) framework. The emphasis is placed on Deep Learning (DL), Convolutional neural networks (CNN), Vision Transformers (ViT), and hybrid sensor assistance-based methods for disease detection and classification. Recent studies show that CNN variants such as VGG16, DenseNet, and EfficientNet have achieved accuracies greater than 95 $\%$, while ensemble models and ConvNeXt-ViT hybrids have reported performance exceeding 95%. Hybrid CNNSVM models and IoT-enabled Systems provide real-time Monitoring and detection capabilities, improve production and enhance field applicability. Also, disease severity estimation models used on ResNet50 and a sensor-based image segmentation enable a mechanism to qualify infection stages, offering deeper agronomic insight. Despite these added efficiencies capability to support decision making at the management level, lightweight interpretable AI models, standardised datasets, and sensor-IoT frameworks into cost-effective solutions for scalable precision agriculture. Real-time detection using AI, Mobile applications, drones and sensors has the potential to minimise yield loss, improve farmer decision-making, as well as support sustainable mango cultivation.
papers.venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing and Electronics Systems (ICCCES)

papers.title: Automated Weed Classification Techniques: Datasets, Methods, and Challenges
papers.abstract: Automated weeding remains a prominent challenge in agriculture domain, and it needs to addressed effectively to improve the crop yield and quality. Traditional methods of weeding (herbicide treatments or manual removal) are often labor-intensive, not affordable, and the chemical control with herbicides causes soil pollution. Recent advancements in deep learning and computer vision techniques, however, have introduced a set of tools that are increasingly proving to be efficient, precise, and largely automated. In this review, we focus on literature sourced from the Stored Literature Collections database, surveying prior studies on state-of-the-art approaches, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), DenseNet architectures, transfer learning, attention mechanisms, and the explainable AI (XAI) framework, all applied to the classification and detection of weeds among cotton, sorghum, and maize crops. The widely employed benchmark weed datasets and its prominent characteristics are reported in the work. The state-of-the-art machine learning and deep learning algorithms employed in automated weeding systems are discussed in detail. The integration of these algorithms with robotics, UAVs, and precision agriculture systems enables minimizing chemical usage and boosting the sustainability of agricultural practices. The work also addresses the potential challenges and feasible solutions in implementing the automated weeding systems on edge devices.
papers.venue: 2026 IEEE 6th International Conference on Computing, Power, and Communication Technologies (IC2PCT)

papers.title: Residual-Enhanced YOLO with Motion-Blur Augmentation for UAV-Based Weed Detection
papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) combined with deep learning models have transformed weed detection in precision agriculture, yet challenges remain in adapting to field variability, limited datasets, and motion blur from UAV flight. While CNNs and Transformer-based methods achieve high accuracy, their deployment often struggles with real-time constraints. YOLO architectures, by contrast, offer a strong balance between inference speed and detection accuracy, making them suitable for in-field use. In this paper, we propose YOLO-Res, a residual-skip enhanced YOLO model tailored for UAV-based weed detection in maize fields under true field conditions. The model incorporates motion-blur augmentation during training to simulate UAV-induced artifacts and leverages residual connections to strengthen feature propagation across scales, thereby improving robustness to degraded inputs. Evaluations on the WeedsGalore dataset demonstrate that YOLO-Res consistently outperforms baseline YOLO variants, achieving superior detection accuracy even under severe blur and varying crop–weed densities, while maintaining real-time inference capability.
papers.venue: Advanced Industrial Conference on Telecommunications

papers.title: Drone-Assisted Deep Learning Framework for Aquatic Weed Detection and Water Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: This research presents a novel deep learning frame-work for evaluating water quality through automated detection of aquatic vegetation in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery. Seven aquatic plant species—Water Hyacinth, Duckweeds, and Water Lettuce among others—served as biological indicators of water conditions. A comprehensive dataset comprising 1,778 aerial photographs was utilized to train and validate multiple object detection architectures, including YOLOv8, Faster R- CNN with MobileNetV2 backbone, Faster R-CNN with ResNet50 backbone, and InceptionV3. Performance evaluation encom- passed mean Average Precision (mAP), processing velocity, and computational efficiency metrics. Experimental findings revealed YOLOv8 as the optimal solution, delivering superior accuracy- performance equilibrium (0.42 mAP at 44.4 FPS), whereas Faster R-CNN with ResNet50 achieved enhanced precision (0.84 mAP) at increased computational cost. The investigation established a comprehensive correlation methodology connecting vegetation characteristics—presence, density, and spatial patterns—to physicochemical water parameters including pH, dissolved oxy- gen concentration, nutrient content, and contamination mark- ers. Comparative validation with conventional water analysis methods yielded robust correlation coefficients ($0.78-0.91$). This methodology represents a dependable, non-destructive technique for comprehensive spatiotemporal water quality surveillance, enabling gradient visualization and temporal trend analysis.
papers.venue: 2025 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Knowledge Economy (ICCIKE)

papers.title: Socially Informed Priority Scoring for Cost-Effective UAV Weed Spraying
papers.abstract: The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in automated weed control is getting more widely used to reduce labour requirements and reduce unnecessary herbicides. The existing systems, however, only optimise on the detection accuracy and do not consider the socio-agronomic priorities on which the real spray decisions in farming practises are made. This study offers a socially informed, cost-conscious priority scoring system that helps the UAVs automatically decide when and where it is appropriate to spray weeds. The pipeline integrates: (i) SAM-ViT-H vegetation mask detection, (ii) species detection with a fine-tuned EfficientNet-B2 classifier, and (iii) an interpretable severity score based on patch size, weed density, and a species-based coefficient that indicates perceived aggressiveness. This coefficient is also learned optionally by crowdsourcing, to coordinate UAV activities with the needs of communities, and enable such stakeholders as farmers, agronomists, and others to articulate the urgency of weeds using comparative rating and via social-media engagement. Experiments on the DeepWeeds dataset show strong operational performance, achieving 95.14% precision, 95.14% recall, >92% weed-coverage recall and only 0.61% false-positive spray activations. The framework improves decision accountability by combining data-driven severity analysis with crowdsourced preference learning of weed species and their aggressiveness. This enables UAVs to balance ecological risk and herbicide expenditure while maintaining human interpretability. By integrating social signals into autonomous spray prioritisation, this work bridges technological capability with user-driven sustainability agendas, advancing the broader adoption of intelligent and publicly aligned precision agriculture.
papers.venue: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development

papers.title: FusionNet-GLD: A Dual-Backbone CNN Model Combining Xception and Inception for Grape Leaf Disease Recognition
papers.abstract: Grapevine leaf diseases like black rot, leaf blight, and esca directly impact vineyard productivity through yield decline and fruit quality deterioration. Early and precise detection will go a long way in efficient management, but conventional manual inspections are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and tend to be unreliable for commercial vineyards.To solve these issues, we introduce FusionNet-GLD, a double-backbone convolutional neural network for the classification of grapevine leaf diseases. It combines Xception and InceptionV3 models to take their complementary advantages. Xception extracts fine-grained patterns through depthwise separable convolutions, whereas InceptionV3 captures features across different scales via small and large convolutional filters. This synergy allows FusionNet-GLD to well capture the intricate visual patterns of affected leaves. The predictive framework was also drilled and assessed on an augmented PlantVillage resource in real vineyard-simulating conditions. The experimental results indicate that FusionNet-GLD beats five baseline models—Random Forest, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0, InceptionV3, and Xception—with 99.63% accuracy, 99.45% precision, 99.42% recall, 99.43% F1score, and 0.99 AUC.These results prove FusionNet-GLD to be efficient, accurate, and scalable. Its lightweight architecture makes it deployable on handheld devices or drones, which will be useful in monitoring vineyards in real time and facilitating precision agriculture by minimizing the use of manual labor and maximizing early disease detection.
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Innovate for Humanitarian: Tech Solutions for Global Challenge (ICIH)

papers.title: Development of a UAV-based crop disease detection system using deep learning algorithms to enhance precision agriculture
papers.abstract: Abstract The shift toward precision agriculture has made it clear that there is a need for smart and automated systems that can detect crop diseases promptly and with high precision. A research project is being discussed here, which presents a comprehensive drone-based solution for detecting cotton leaf disease, combining the latest advances in deep learning with the gradual training of the machine for rapid decision-making in agriculture. In the beginning, the system implements adaptive median filtering (AMF), followed by the contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) process, which removes noise and enhances the image’s contrast. The Swin Transformer is used to identify spatial and spectral features at different levels, while the combination of ConvNeXt-V2 and the squeeze-and-excitation blocks with bidirectional long short-term memory (SE-BiLSTM) classifier refines spatial cues and learns sequential dependencies for precise disease classification. Moreover, the framework includes a Deep Q-Learning (DQL) recommendation module that supplies contextually aware crop management activities, like the optimized use of pesticides and scheduling of irrigation. The experimental results, derived from the SAR-CLD-2024 dataset, indicate a remarkable performance with an accuracy of 99.30%, thereby surpassing existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based and hybrid models in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. The combination of deep learning with reinforcement learning in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based systems indicates a future of sustainable, adaptable, and data-driven precision agriculture.
papers.venue: International Journal on Smart Sensing and Intelligent Systems

papers.title: State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Algorithms for Internet of Things-Based Detection of Crop Pests and Diseases: A Comprehensive Review
papers.abstract: Plant pest and disease management, especially in the early stages of infestation, is a critical challenge that poses significant threats and has potential to devastate agricultural crops, causing total yield loss and food insecurity. Traditional inspection methods are time-consuming and prone to errors due to limited labor expertise. Therefore, to tackle these challenges, harnessing advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), Machine Learning/Deep Learning (ML/DL), and Internet of Things (IoT) is essential for managing and mitigating agriculture hazards. This research presents a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art DL architectures integrated with IoT-based systems applied to plant pest and disease detection (PPDD) by investigating different potential approaches that have been employed using DL and IoT up to the year 2024 to address challenges in agriculture. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures for image recognition, object detection, and their integration with IoT, embedded into mobile devices and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) are explored. Moreover, the research discusses the advantages and limitations of these techniques, emphasizing their architecture design, efficiency and accuracy. The findings demonstrate that there is a tradeoff between robustness and complexity among existing techniques, and authors recommend future trends aimed at creating robust models with fewer parameters that are more accurate and easily implementable on small IoT-based and portable devices suitable for in-field and real-time applications. Furthermore, while existing review papers discuss either DL or IoT separately, this research paper uniquely focuses on their combined models, providing a comprehensive overview of the synergistic potential of leveraging IoT-driven technologies alongside advanced DL algorithms to ease the task of researchers in the field of precision agriculture particularly in PPDD.
papers.venue: IEEE Access

papers.title: Intelligent Weed Management in Paddy Fields via Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Weeds in paddy fields are detected and removed using computer vision and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to develop an intelligent automated system. Paddy productivity is significantly affected by weed infestation, as weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients, and sunlight, thereby reducing crop yield and quality. Traditional weed management methods, particularly chemical-based approaches, are associated with environmental pollution and increased production costs. To address these challenges, the proposed system employs image processing techniques along with a CNN-based classification model to differentiate weeds from paddy crops. High-resolution field images captured using drones or ground-based cameras are preprocessed and segmented to extract discriminative features for accurate weed identification. Once weeds are detected, targeted removal techniques such as robotic arms or precision herbicide spraying are applied to minimize crop damage. Experimental results demonstrate that the developed CNN model is feasible for multi-convolutional weed classification under diverse field conditions. The system proves to be effective and robust, promoting reduced labor dependency, lower herbicide usage, and decreased environmental impact. Overall, the proposed framework supports sustainable and cost-effective paddy cultivation through intelligent and automated precision agriculture.
papers.venue: International Conferences on Information Science and System

papers.title: Automated Detection and Detterents of Harmful Birds in Tomato Cultivation
papers.abstract: This work introduces an autonomous learning system for preventing bird damage in tomato crops based on state-of-the-art computer vision and machine learning. The system applies Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Random Forest (RF) for real-time bird detection and classification. Ensemble learning enhances accuracy, minimizing crop loss at the cost of being cost-effective. The research compares different methods, such as deep learning-based deterrent systems and Internet of Things (IoT) solutions. Comparison with conventional bird-scaring methods is made to show the benefits of automation. Experimental evidence confirms the effectiveness of the system and proves its potential application in precision agriculture. The improvements for the future involve the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and IoT-based interventions to further improve scalability.
papers.venue: International Congress on Information and Communication Technology

papers.title: Attention-Enhanced GCN with SPP for UAV-Captured Plant Imagery
papers.abstract: Global agricultural productivity faces severe threats from plant diseases, which demand the development of effective and scalable detection methods. Traditional methods like manual inspection combined with handcrafted feature extraction demand extensive labor while proving ineffective for large-scale applications. The combined progress in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology and deep learning (DL) now supports automated disease detection, yet current techniques fail to represent intricate spatial relationships and dependencies within plant images, which restricts their performance. This research document introduces an innovative framework that combines Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) with attention mechanisms, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP), and skip connections to tackle UAV-based plant disease classification challenges. This framework utilizes multiple Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract robust features while integrating multi-scale features through SPP and refining them with GCNs that include attention mechanisms and skip connections. The results from 5-fold cross-validation demonstrate the framework’s remarkable validation accuracy of 97.61%, F1-score of 0. 9848, the precision of 0. 9857, and recall of 0. 9842. These results achieve substantial performance gains over EfficientNet-B0 ShuffleNetV2 ResNet-18 and a basic GCN without attention. Significantly, the GCN with attention surpasses the simple GCN by around 2.4% in validation accuracy. This research demonstrates that integrating UAV imagery with advanced DL models establishes scalable soybean disease detection, laying the groundwork for precision agriculture applications.
papers.venue: 2025 International Conference on Computing, Intelligence, and Application (CIACON)

papers.title: Multispectral Image Analysis for Agricultural Crop Classification in Peru Using Deep Learning Techniques
papers.abstract: Crop classification is crucial for agricultural management, especially in the context of precision agriculture in Peru. This study presents the results of three investigations that utilize remote sensing and deep learning technologies to classify agricultural crops across different phenological phases. Using multispectral images obtained from UAVs and satellites, the study focuses on classifying table grapes, corn and quinoa crops, three key agro-exportable products in Peru. The research emphasizes the use of semantic segmentation networks in conjunction with vegetation indices such as NDVI to improve the accuracy of crop classification. The results demonstrate that deep learning techniques outperform traditional classification methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, particularly when integrating various image types and addressing phenological variations. This work aims to optimize crop management and resource use while contributing to food security through better decision-making based on geospatial data.
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE Afro-Mediterranean Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AMCAI)

papers.title: Recent Trends in AI and Data Science for Smart and Sustainable Agriculture: Enhancing Global Food Security
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science (DS) are revolutionizing agriculture by enabling precision farming, predictive analytics, and resource optimization to address food security amid climate challenges and population growth. This review paper explores recent trends (2023–2026) in smart and sustainable agriculture, focusing on AI applications in crop monitoring, yield prediction, pest detection, smart irrigation, and climate-resilient decision support. Key technologies—machine learning (e.g., CNNs, RNNs), computer vision, IoT integration, drones, and satellite imagery—are analyzed through a systematic literature review of 50+ recent papers, highlighting their impact on yield improvement (up to 20–30%), resource savings (e.g., 90% less herbicides), and sustainability metrics like reduced emissions and water use. Case studies demonstrate real-world deployments, such as AI-driven yield mapping and autonomous weeding. Challenges including data scarcity, high costs for smallholders, model interpretability, and ethical concerns are discussed, alongside future directions like multimodal AI, edge computing, and federated learning for equitable access. By synthesizing these advancements, this paper underscores AI's pivotal role in achieving UN Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger) through data-driven, resilient farming systems.
papers.venue: International Journal of Engineering and Management Research

papers.title: AI-Powered Crop Disease Detection: An Integrated Approach to Plant Disease and Insect Classification
papers.abstract: Effective management of plant diseases and pests is crucial for ensuring agricultural productivity and minimizing economic losses. Traditional detection methods are often slow, labor-intensive, and prone to inaccuracies. This paper presents an AI-based system that leverages deep learning to accurately detect plant diseases and classify pests from images. The proposed approach utilizes the VGG16 architecture with transfer learning, trained on two distinct datasets from Kaggle: one containing approximately 87,000 RGB images across 38 plant disease classes and another comprising about 3100 RGB images for 9 different pests. Image preprocessing techniques, including resizing to 224×224 pixels and normalization, were applied to improve model performance. A newer approach for training the disease detection models is used. VGG16 model was adapted by replacing the fully connected layers with custom dense layers tailored for classification tasks. The system was trained using the Adam optimizer and evaluated on metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, demonstrating high performance in both disease and pest classification. A user-friendly web and mobile interface enable users to upload or capture images for real-time analysis. Upon detection, the system provides detailed reports, treatment suggestions, and direct purchase links for recommended pesticides. Future developments aim to incorporate drone integration, and advanced models like Vision Transformers (ViTs) to enhance accuracy, precision and scalability. This research highlights the potential of AI-driven approaches in advancing precision agriculture and promoting sustainable farming practices.
papers.venue: 2025 Third International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)

papers.title: Deep Learning with Particle Swarm Based Hyper Parameter Tuning Based Crop Recommendation for Better Crop Yield for Precision Agriculture
papers.abstract: The common diﬃculty present among the Indian farmers is that they don’t opt for the proper crop based on their soil necessities. Because of this productivity is aﬀected. This problem of the farmers has been solved through precision agriculture. This method is characterized by a crop database collected from the farm, crop provided by agricultural experts and given to recommendation system it will use the collect data and do deep learning model as learners to recommend a crop for site speciﬁc parameter with high accuracy and eﬃciency. Objectives : The comprehensive objective of the model is to deliver direct advisory services to even the smallest farmer at the level of his/her smallest plot of crop, using the most accessible technologies using deep learning. It is a recommender model built using a classiﬁer and an optimization of the classiﬁer. Based on appropriate parameters, the prediction accuracy. Novelty : MDNN can produce to simpler models while working with weights that can be optimized through PSO. PSO-MDNN sub-models produced from datasets and this proposed models gets adapted to data patterns if featuring datasets. This proposed work also exhibits promising outcomes in predicting crop yields using DLTs. for classifying images build a crop yield prediction model based on NDVI (New band Index)/RGB (Red Green Blue) data from UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles). The study evaluated the results of CNN by varying its parameters like training algorithm, network depth/layers, regularizations and tuning of hyper parameters.

papers.title: A Deep Learning System Based on YOLO for Finding Insects in Precision Agriculture
papers.abstract: Managing pests on farms is an important part of Food security and modern ways to protect crops. This study introduces a YOLO-based deep learning framework for realtime agricultural pest detection utilizing the YOLOv8 architecture Roboflow exported an annotated pest dataset that had five pest categories: weevil, caterpillar, grasshopper, slug, and snail. The suggested system's mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) for all pest classes is 0.952. The AP scores for each class range from 0.849 for caterpillars to 0.995 for snails and grasshoppers. To make sure that the framework works well in a variety of field situations, It uses data augmentation methods, decoupled anchor-free detection heads, and multi-scale feature pyramid networks. Tests on Google Colab's GPU infrastructure show that the system works much better than baseline models like YOLOv5 and Faster R-CNN, which can process more than 60 frames per second in real time with good accuracy and speed. Some uses are automated systems for monitoring crops, drones for field surveillance, and platforms for precision agriculture, and smart farms can get help and advice. Future research will focus on expanding the framework to include additional crop and pest species, along with more advanced YOLO variants and getting it to work on edge devices with limited resources.
papers.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems in Engineering, Secured Systems and Cybersecurity (ICISESSC)

# PRISMA 2020 Screening — Batch 43/60

You are performing a systematic literature review screening step.
Evaluate EACH paper below against the protocol criteria.

## Research Questions
- **RQ1**: What is the comparative segmentation performance (mIoU, F1-score) of CNNs, Transformers, and Hybrid architectures on agricultural UAV crop-weed imagery, specifically in paired intra-study benchmarks?
- **RQ2**: How do edge hardware constraints (thermal design power, compute capacity in TOPS) and execution configurations (quantization precision, input resolution) impact real-time inference throughput (FPS, latency) for UAV segmentation models?

## Inclusion Criteria (must match to INCLUDE)
- **INC-01**: Focuses on deep learning architectures (CNN, Transformer, or Hybrid) applied to UAV aerial imagery for agricultural crop/weed pixel-level segmentation.
- **INC-02**: Reports quantitative pixel-wise segmentation accuracy metrics (e.g., mIoU, class IoU, Dice/F1-score) on agricultural benchmark or custom UAV datasets.
- **INC-03**: Reports on-device empirical hardware execution metrics (e.g., FPS, latency in ms, power in Watts, memory footprint) on physical edge platforms or embedded accelerators.

## Exclusion Criteria (any match → EXCLUDE)
- **EXC-01** (OUT_OF_SCOPE_MODALITY): Non-UAV imaging modalities (satellite-only, ground-vehicle/tractor-only, or laboratory bench-top setups without aerial flight context).
- **EXC-02** (OUT_OF_SCOPE_TASK): Bounding-box object detection or whole-image classification without pixel-level semantic or instance segmentation masks.
- **EXC-03** (OUT_OF_SCOPE_DOMAIN): Agricultural domains outside crop and weed management (e.g., orchard fruit counting, forestry canopy height, livestock tracking, soil moisture estimation).
- **EXC-04** (METHODOLOGICAL_MISMATCH): Exclusively non-deep learning methods (e.g., classical vegetation indices like ExG/NDVI with Otsu thresholding or shallow SVM without learned features).
- **EXC-05** (SECONDARY_LITERATURE): Secondary literature without primary empirical benchmarks (surveys, systematic reviews, viewpoint letters, or tutorials).
- **EXC-06** (INSUFFICIENT_DATA): Non-English text or records lacking retrievable quantitative results.
